policy_or_incentive: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry
official_finding: MoFPI states PLISFPI has an outlay of Rs 10,900 crore, supports creation of global food manufacturing champions, covers RTE/RTC including millet-based products, processed fruits and vegetables, marine products and mozzarella cheese, and runs for 2021-22 to 2026-27.
relevance_to_investigation: Shows food-processing policy actively encourages scale, capacity expansion, branding abroad, and large manufacturing platforms, which can attract institutional capital.
limitations_or_caveats: Policy objectives are not evidence of PE causation or harm; beneficiary-level ownership mapping is still needed.

official_finding: PIB/MoFPI reports 168 approved applicants, cumulative investment of about Rs 9,207 crore, around 35 LMT per annum processing/preservation capacity, and Rs 2,714.79 crore incentives disbursed.
relevance_to_investigation: Provides a measurable incentive-policy baseline for food manufacturing and packaged-food expansion.
limitations_or_caveats: Applicant list, ownership class, product-level nutrition effects and price effects are not mapped here.

policy_or_incentive: PLISFPI beneficiary mix and manufacturing-location condition
official_finding: PIB/MoFPI reports 69 MSME applicants, 40 MSME contract manufacturing units of main applicants, two cooperatives, two innovative-food applicants and 13 organic-sector applicants; incentives require the entire manufacturing chain including primary processing to take place in India.
relevance_to_investigation: Relevant to domestic capacity and supply-chain localization; not simply a foreign-capital subsidy.
limitations_or_caveats: Does not show whether foreign institutional investors own any approved applicants or contract manufacturers.

official_finding: PIB/MoFPI reports PMKSY FY 2024-25 allocation of Rs 630 crore and states grants-in-aid are available to eligible entities including public and private sector companies, proprietorship firms, partnerships, LLPs, cooperatives, FPOs/FPCs and SHGs for food processing, preservation, testing and R&D infrastructure.
relevance_to_investigation: Shows explicit public financial support for private-sector food-processing and supply-chain infrastructure.
limitations_or_caveats: Grant recipients and ownership class are not mapped here; public/private eligibility does not imply PE-specific benefit.

policy_or_incentive: PMKSY project outcomes and cold-chain infrastructure
official_finding: PIB/MoFPI reports that as of 30 June 2025 PMKSY had 1,601 projects approved, 1,133 completed or operationalized, Rs 5,365.32 crore approved grant, 255.66 LMT per annum preservation/processing capacity, 34,15,102 farmers benefited and 4,33,639 employment generated. It also reports 395 integrated cold-chain/value-addition projects approved.
relevance_to_investigation: Relevant to cold-chain, value-addition and farmer-benefit claims; it shows intended capacity and farmer benefits, not ownership-linked outcomes.
limitations_or_caveats: Reported beneficiaries are official scheme outputs; independent impact evaluation and PE-recipient classification remain missing.

official_finding: PIB/MoFPI release says MIDH post-harvest infrastructure assistance is credit-linked back-ended subsidy at 35 percent of project cost in general areas and 50 percent in hilly and scheduled areas through State Horticulture Missions.
relevance_to_investigation: Shows public support for post-harvest infrastructure that can alter cold-chain economics and private participation.
limitations_or_caveats: MIDH is not PE-specific and is administered through agriculture/horticulture channels, not only MoFPI.

official_finding: Income Tax Department guidance says Section 35AD specified businesses include setting up and operating a cold-chain facility, warehousing for agricultural produce, and building and operating a hospital with at least 100 beds.
relevance_to_investigation: Shows tax policy can improve after-tax economics for infrastructure-heavy hospital, cold-chain and agri-warehousing projects.
limitations_or_caveats: The document is official guidance but says it is not a legal document; detailed applicability requires Act/Rules and transaction-level tax analysis.

official_finding: The reviewed incentives are capacity-building and manufacturing/supply-chain policies available to eligible entities, including private companies. They can make investment more attractive but do not prove that policy was designed for foreign PE or that PE caused adverse outcomes.
relevance_to_investigation: Prevents overclaiming: policy enablement and investment incentives are causal preconditions, not proof of capture or harm.
limitations_or_caveats: Beneficiary ownership mapping, deal-level tax analysis, treaty application and private fund documents remain incomplete.

official_finding: SEBI's 2012 press release says all AIFs, including private equity funds, real estate funds and hedge funds, must register with SEBI. It describes Category II AIFs as including private equity funds, debt funds and funds of funds, without specific government or regulator incentives or concessions, and without leverage except for permitted day-to-day operational requirements.
relevance_to_investigation: Provides the domestic pooled-fund regulatory baseline for Indian PE/AIF structures. It weakens claims that domestic Category II PE funds are unregulated or receive Category II-specific incentives.
limitations_or_caveats: Does not map individual LPs, offshore feeder funds, side letters or healthcare/food investee-level rights.

official_finding: IFSCA's 2025 Fund Management Regulations state that an entity cannot commence fund-management operations in IFSC without IFSCA FME registration. Registration categories include Authorised FME, Registered FME Non-Retail and Registered FME Retail; Registered FME Non-Retail can pool money by private placement through restricted schemes and can file Category II AIF schemes for investments outside Category I and III strategies.
relevance_to_investigation: Provides a current GIFT IFSC fund-structuring framework relevant to foreign and domestic institutional capital, including private-placement non-retail schemes.
limitations_or_caveats: Does not prove that any specific healthcare or food transaction used a GIFT IFSC vehicle or obtained specific tax benefits.

policy_or_incentive: IFSC capital-gains and offshore-fund relocation provisions
official_finding: Income Tax Department section 47 text states that specified non-resident transfers on recognized IFSC exchanges paid in foreign currency and offshore-fund relocation transfers under clauses (viiac)/(viiad) are not regarded as transfers under specified conditions. The IFSCA brochure reports 23 relocated schemes, US$9.14bn cumulative commitments, US$3.56bn funds raised and US$4.38bn cumulative investments as of September 30, 2025, and summarizes tax-neutral relocation benefits.
relevance_to_investigation: Shows a real fund-relocation and IFSC tax-policy architecture that can influence fund domiciliation and routing choices.
evidence_classification: VERIFIED FACT for framework and IFSCA-reported scale; EXPERT INTERPRETATION for investment-routing relevance
limitations_or_caveats: The brochure is promotional and not legal advice; Income Tax application is condition-specific; sector-level beneficiary mapping and treaty analysis are not complete.
